instruction:
Simulation Zone Confetti. `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` contains: - A mesh plane `Emitter` centered at world (0, 0, 5), scaled to span a 4x4 BU square at z = 5. - A mesh plane `Ground` centered at world (0, 0, 0), scaled 10x10 BU (visual only). - Scene fps = 24, frame range [1, 60], current frame = 1. - `Emitter` has NO geometry nodes modifier yet. Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal. For this task, use `/opt/blender/blender` for Blender command-line or background runs when working on `scene.blend`.

Add a Geometry Nodes modifier on `Emitter` that uses a Simulation Zone to emit and integrate ballistic "confetti" points every frame. Do NOT apply the modifier - it must remain on the modifier stack. Required behaviour: 1. Inside the Geometry Nodes tree, create a Simulation Zone (paired `Simulation Input` and `Simulation Output` nodes). The zone's persistent state is a single GEOMETRY item. 2. Feed the Simulation Input's initial-state geometry from an EMPTY point cloud (e.g. a `Points` node with Count = 0) so the simulation starts with zero points at frame 1. 3. Each step INSIDE the simulation zone must do the following, in order: A. Read the per-point `velocity` attribute (FLOAT_VECTOR, POINT domain) via an Input Named Attribute node; when the attribute is absent the input falls back to (0, 0, 0) automatically. B. Update velocity: new_vel = velocity + gravity * delta_time, where gravity = (0, 0, -9.81). Use the `Delta Time` output of the Simulation Input node for `delta_time`. C. Update position: new_pos = position + new_vel * delta_time. D. Clamp to ground: if new_pos.z < 0 then new_pos.z = 0 AND new_vel.z = 0 (use Compare + Switch or Math Maximum to clamp). E. Apply the clamped position via Set Position, and store the clamped velocity back on the POINT domain via a Store Named Attribute node with name = "velocity", data_type = FLOAT_VECTOR, domain = POINT. 4. Also INSIDE the simulation zone, emit exactly 10 NEW points per frame: - A `Points` node with Count = 10, with each new point placed at a random (x, y, 5) with x, y uniformly in [-2, 2] (i.e. within the emitter plane). - Each new point is given an initial `velocity` attribute of (rand_x in [-3, 3], rand_y in [-3, 3], 3): horizontal scatter up to 3 BU/s, plus a constant +3 BU/s upward kick. Store this as a FLOAT_VECTOR POINT-domain named attribute `velocity` on the new points. - Each frame must emit distinct random values (use Scene Time.Frame to shift the Random Value node's ID input so the emissions on different frames are not identical). 5. Still INSIDE the zone, join the physics-updated existing points with the newly emitted 10 points via `Join Geometry`, and feed the joined geometry into the Simulation Output (Geometry state). No points are ever deleted, so after N frames the simulation holds exactly 10*N points. 6. OUTSIDE the zone, convert the Simulation Output's point cloud into a mesh via `Points to Vertices` (this preserves the POINT-domain `velocity` attribute as a vertex attribute on the evaluated mesh), and plug the mesh into the Group Output. Save the completed scene as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. ## Requirements 1. `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` exists and opens as a valid Blender file. 2. `Emitter` exists as a mesh object and carries exactly one Geometry Nodes (NODES) modifier, and no other modifiers. 3. The node tree contains at least one `GeometryNodeSimulationInput` AND at least one `GeometryNodeSimulationOutput`. 4. After stepping the scene from frame 1 up to frame 30, the evaluated mesh on `Emitter` has 300 vertices +/- 5% (i.e. 285..315 inclusive). 5. Every vertex has z >= 0 (tolerance 1e-3 below). 6. The evaluated mesh carries a POINT-domain FLOAT_VECTOR attribute named `velocity`. 7. Ballistic distribution sanity at frame 30: at least one vertex has z > 4.5 (a recently emitted point near the emitter), at least one vertex has z < 3.0 (an older point that has been falling), and no vertex is above z = 6.0 (matches the physical peak of ~ 5.46 BU reached by a point with initial v_z = 3 under gravity = 9.81).
